browserActions.title: Browser actions
browserActions.envVarLabel: Variable holding the text to type

role.loggedIn: Wait until you are logged in

browserActions.persistentSessionAdvanced: Advanced: stay logged in between runs

headers.text: Extra headers the script sends with every request, e.g. a language, a Referer or an API key. For a secret, choose "Environment variable" and enter only its name; the test value is used for the trial run only and is never saved. A header named User-Agent replaces the default one.

picker.text: Pick what the header is for: the name and a suggestion are filled in for you. Secrets (Cookie, Authorization, API key) start as an environment variable, so they never end up in the script. "Other" lets you type any header name.

append.text: Each run adds its rows to the output file the earlier runs left, so the file grows into an archive. If the fields change, the file keeps its columns and new ones are added; a file that cannot be read stops the run without being touched. Not available in combined mode.

causes.text:
Not started → start it, then press "Try again".
Other port or computer → enter its address below.
Another computer → the address must start with https://.
Shared companion → it may need an access key (Settings).

choice.text:
Fields — a plain list, the same few values per item (a product list).
Containers — items with sub-items (a menu: categories → dishes).
API — the page loads its data from a hidden request; try it when Fields find nothing.
Combined, Blocks — several saved scrapers in one script, or several files from one page.

type.text:
Single element — it exists once on the page (e.g. the page header).
Repeating — it appears many times (e.g. every dish of a menu); you get one result per match.

container.text:
Text — the visible text (a price).
Attribute — a value from the tag (a link's address or an image's source).
Exists? — only whether the element is there (a "sale" badge).
Own text only — the element's own text without nested elements (a name without its badge).

flat.text:
Text — the visible text (a price).
Attribute — a value from the tag (a link's address or an image's source, e.g. to download it).

choice.text:
Static — fast; reads the page as the server sends it.
Browser — a real browser; for pages built by JavaScript, with a login, or that need scrolling.
When Static finds nothing, Browser is usually the fix.

what.text: A named value stored on the computer that runs the script — a safe place for passwords and keys, so they never end up in the script. Enter only its name here (e.g. SMTP_PASSWORD); the script reads the value when it runs, on that computer — not in the browser.
what.example:
Windows:  setx SMTP_PASSWORD "secret"
macOS/Linux:  export SMTP_PASSWORD="secret"

regex.text: Pick a recipe and the pattern is written for you — your text is taken literally, so symbols like . or ( are fine. The pattern stays editable; “Part to keep” is which bracketed part of it becomes the value (0 = the whole match).

dateFormat.text: Describe how the date is written: {dd} is the day, {mm} the month, {yyyy} the year, everything else exactly as it appears. Only numeric dates work — month names like “Aug” don't.

overview.text: Steps applied to the value before it is written — for example trim it, extract a number or convert it to a date. Save a chain as a preset to reuse it on other fields.

severity.text: Checks run at the end of every run of the script. “Warn me”: the run finishes normally and a message is printed. “Stop the run”: the run is marked as failed, so a scheduler or monitoring tool notices — exit code 2 (an unexpected crash is code 1).

recommended.text: Switches on a sensible start: a warning when nothing was found at all, and a warning for rows missing their first field (those rows are left out of the file). Checks you already set are left alone.

noResult.text: Warns when the script found nothing at all — usually because the website changed its layout.
noResult.example: The selector for “Price” suddenly matches no element.

nullRate.text: Warns when too many rows have no value in one field: the selector still finds something, but not the right thing.
nullRate.example: Warn when more than 50 % of the rows have no Price.

baseline.text: Warns when this run found much less than the last run — a broken “load more” button or pagination often looks like this.

blocking.text: Warns when the site starts blocking the script but still answers normally: it sends you to another website, sends a very short page, or shows a block message.

blockingAdvanced.text: A block page is usually tiny: 1000 bytes is about one paragraph of text. Phrases are searched in the page, one per line; any hit counts as blocked.
blockingAdvanced.example:
Access Denied
Please verify you are human

requiredFields.text: Leaves out every row that has no value for the chosen fields, so incomplete rows never reach the file. The rest of the run carries on.
requiredFields.example: A database import that needs a non-empty Price.

overview.text: A login is four steps: fill in the user name, fill in the password, click the login button, then wait until the logged-in page appears. The steps run in the order listed, before any data is read. “Login form” adds all four at once — you only click the elements on the page.
overview.example: Fill user name → Fill password → Click “Log in” → Wait for “Welcome back”

maxRounds.text: How many times the script scrolls down or clicks “Load more” before it stops. A higher number loads more items but takes longer; it also stops early once nothing new appears.

persistentSession.text: After a run the script saves your cookies and login state in a file next to its output and, next time, skips the login steps above. The file holds live session cookies: treat it like a password and never share or commit it. If the session expires the run simply fails — there is no automatic re-login; delete the file to log in again.

urlTemplate.text: The address pattern for pages 2, 3, …: {page} is replaced by the page number, {url} (optional) by the start page exactly as it is. Page 1 is always the start page itself. With several start pages {url} is required.

maxPages.text: A safety limit: the script stops after this many pages even if there are more. It also stops earlier as soon as a page has no results or the “Next” link is gone.

overview.text: For sites whose list of pages changes, e.g. a category menu: the script opens this page once, collects every link that matches the selector and scrapes each linked page as an extra start page. Pick one link in the menu — the selector then fits all similar links. A link can also be chosen by its text.

urlParts.text: Each part of the address either stays fixed or changes between requests. Tick "variable" for a part that takes different values — a week, a category, a page — and give it a name; below you say where its values come from. Parts left fixed are sent exactly as recorded.

bodyVariable.text: A value in the request body is fixed or changes between requests. "→ Variable" lets it take the values of a parameter (a new one or an existing one), e.g. the category of a search request.

valueType.text: How the value is written into the body. Text fits most APIs; choose Number or Boolean when the server expects a number or true/false — a quoted "10" would be rejected.

sourceStaticList.text: You type the values yourself, or collect them from the recording; the script requests every one of them.

sourceDiscovery.text: The values come from another request the site makes, e.g. a list of categories. Click one of those values on the page and the matching request is found for you. When you edit its address, the "insert parameter" list adds {name} at the cursor — move it to where a fixed value would go, e.g. .../categories/{category}/weeks.
sourceDiscovery.example: GET /api/categories  →  every id in the list

sourceRange.text: Counts through a range: ISO weeks, plain numbers or dates.

sourceBrowserDiscovery.text: For values that only show up while the page is used: the script opens a browser, performs your clicks and scrolls and notes which values the site requests.
sourceBrowserDiscovery.example: scroll the offers page, collect each category name

sourceBootstrap.text: This part of the address takes the freshly fetched login token (see "the API needs a login token first").

fields.text: The fields to extract from the response. A group scopes its fields to a list or object in the JSON; a field is one value.

overview.text: For APIs that need a short-lived token from a login/token request first. The script sends that request at the start of every run and uses the extracted value in the headers/URL below — credentials only ever come from environment variables.

placeholder.text: Use the name in braces, e.g. {token}, in a header ("From token" mode) or pick "Token value" as the value source of a URL part. Requests for a list of values reuse the headers.

overview.text: For APIs that only reveal the next page's cursor inside the current response (e.g. pageInfo.endCursor or next_page_token). The script fetches page after page for every parameter combination until no cursor is returned. Page 1 is sent exactly as recorded, so make sure the recorded request is the first page, without a cursor.

For APIs (GitHub, GitLab, WordPress, ...) that announce the next page in the HTTP Link response header instead of in the body. The script requests that URL page after page for every parameter combination until no next link is left. Not for POST requests. Page 1 is sent exactly as recorded, so make sure the recorded request is the first page. Next-page links to another host are never followed.

A saved list of column names in a fixed order. Pick one and map each column to one of your fields — every column needs a source before the script can be generated; groups of a tree layout are placed automatically. So every export for the same pipeline has the same columns, whichever site it came from.
overview.example: Standard product export: name, price, link

manage.text: An output layout is a saved, reusable list of column names. Create one here, then pick it in a scraper's settings to rename and reorder its output columns.

overview.text: Checks the script runs by itself after every run: found nothing? A field always empty? Far fewer rows than last time? Blocked by the site? It warns you, or marks the run as failed so a scheduler notices.
Before the real run, the script asks the page one cheap question: has it changed since last time? If not, the run is skipped. Pages that don't say so are always scraped.

Drops an item when one with the same key already appeared — in this run, or (if you choose) in an earlier one. Pick the field(s) that identify an item (together they form its key), e.g. an article number. Items whose key fields are all empty are never removed.

incremental.text: The script remembers the keys it has seen in a small file next to its output (output file name + .dedup-seen.json); delete that file to start over. The remembered keys are limited by number or age. The file is only updated after a run that did not fail a safety check.

overview.text: The file the generated script writes. SQLite and Excel contain one table; nested results are flattened into it. Excel needs the Python package openpyxl on the computer that runs the script and on the companion's. Not available for blocks or combined mode, or together with change detection.

flatten.text: Nested results are flattened into one table: one row per innermost item, with values from higher levels repeated in every row. Every data field needs a unique name — or pick an output layout to choose the columns yourself.

overview.text: Lets you change the start URLs, the output name or a field's output name later in a small XML file next to the script — without touching the .py file. The script creates the file the first time it runs.

The script is handed over without being run once against the live page. It is still checked for structural problems, but a wrong selector or a blocked request only shows when you run it yourself, and there is no data preview or full output file.
Fixed name: pre-fills the script name of every new scraper. From website: the name is derived from the current site's address each time. You can still change it per scraper.

forgot.text: Enter your user name or the verified email address of your account. If it has one, a code is sent there; enter it below with a new password.

overview.text: The password goes only to your companion; this browser keeps just a revocable token for this device. Use an https:// companion or one on this computer so the password can't be read on the way.

Only needed if the companion you connect to requires a personal access key (several people sharing one companion). Whoever runs the companion creates it for you. It is stored in this browser and sent with every request.
Only exists in a development build. For a self-signed certificate: open the companion address in a browser tab once (button above), accept the warning, then reload this panel.
Save a transformation chain from a field's dialog with "Save as preset", then apply it to any field via "Apply preset …". Built-in presets are read-only; your own can be renamed or deleted here.
Everything you saved for any site. Load a configuration from the panel on that site's own page; here you can browse its saved outputs or delete entries.

panel.text: Configurations you saved for this site. Load one to restore its setup, or open its saved outputs.

overview.text: Merges several of your own saved configurations — even from different sites — into one script. Their outputs are combined into a single result.
Build several independent extraction blocks (flat or container, freely mixed) on this page. They share one navigation and each writes its own output file in one run. At least 2 blocks are needed.

Enter the name of an environment variable that holds a comma-separated list of proxy URLs, e.g. http://user:pass@host:port — not the addresses themselves. With several proxies the script uses them in turn.

The script waits between two requests — fixed, or random within a range (e.g. 1 to 3 seconds) — to avoid blocks and rate limits. The run takes correspondingly longer (50 pages × 2 s ≈ 1.5 minutes more). The trial run doesn't count the pauses against its time limit.

crawlDelay.text: If the site's robots.txt asks for a pace (Crawl-delay or Request-rate), the script waits at least that long between two requests. Combined with "Pause between requests", the larger gap wins. Sites that publish nothing are unaffected.

disallow.text: While it runs, the script checks every request (pages, further pages, downloads, API calls) against the site's robots.txt Disallow rules — in case the site changed them after you created the script. A robots.txt that can't be read never blocks anything; no robots.txt means no restrictions.

overview.text: After a connection error, a timeout or one of the status codes, the script tries again after the wait (for 429/503 as long as the server asks via Retry-After, at most 60 s). Other errors such as 404 or 403 fail at once. If every attempt fails, the run stops.
Every field here is the name of an environment variable, not its value — the real value is read from the environment when the script runs and is never written into the script.

intro.text: Only useful if you run the script again and again, e.g. every night: it tells you when the website changed and your script stopped working.

overview.text: For similar elements (buttons, links) that only their label tells apart. Capitals and extra spaces don't matter. Leave empty to keep the selection as it is.
A combined or split field is computed from other fields of the same group, not from the page. "Remove the original fields" hides the sources from the output while still using them.

noData.title: No data was found
noData.hint: The selectors matched nothing the script could read. Check the highlighted elements with “Show preview”.
noData.hintStatic: The selectors matched nothing the script could read. Check the highlighted elements with “Show preview”. If the page builds its content with JavaScript, try the Browser engine.

noOutput.title: The script produced no result file
noOutput.hint: It stopped before writing any data. Details shows what happened.

siteUnreachable.title: The site can't be reached
siteUnreachable.hint: Check the page address and your internet connection (and the proxy, if you use one).

siteForbidden.title: The site refuses the script
siteForbidden.hint: It needs a login or blocks automated requests. Use the Browser engine with a login flow, or send a request header such as a cookie.

pageNotFound.title: The page was not found
pageNotFound.hint: Check the page address at the top of the panel.

rateLimited.title: The site says: too many requests
rateLimited.hint: Turn on “Pause between requests” in Settings, or try again later.

siteError.title: The site reported an error
siteError.hint: This is usually temporary. Try again later, or turn on “Retry on transient errors” in Settings.

httpError.title: The site answered with an error (HTTP {status})
httpError.hint: Details has the exact answer. Check the page address and try again.

pageLoadTimeout.title: The page took too long to load
pageLoadTimeout.hint: Try again. If the page works in your browser, it may just be slow.

pageLoadFailed.title: The page could not be loaded
pageLoadFailed.hint: Check the page address and your connection, then try again.

missingEnvVar.title: The script needs the variable {name}
missingEnvVar.hint: Enter a test value next to the field that uses it so the trial run can proceed, and set the variable on the computer where you run the script.

trialTimeout.title: The trial run took too long
trialTimeout.hint: Use fewer pages or requests, or turn on “Skip the trial run” in Settings.

robotsDisallowed.title: The site's robots.txt forbids this request
robotsDisallowed.hint: Choose “Skip it and carry on” or “Warn, but request it anyway” in Settings, or leave this page out.

pythonMissing.title: Python was not found
pythonMissing.hint: The companion needs Python 3.9 or newer to test your script. Install it (or run the installer again), then try again.

packageMissing.title: A Python package is missing
packageMissing.hint: Install it with “pip install {name}” on the computer running the companion (the installer does this for you).

scriptCrash.title: The script stopped with an error
scriptCrash.hint: Details shows the technical message. If it looks like a bug, use “Report bug”.

companionUnreachable.title: The companion app can't be reached
companionUnreachable.hint: Check that it is still running, then try again.

companionError.title: The companion app had a problem
companionError.hint: Try again. If it keeps happening, use “Report bug”.

invalidStartUrl.title: The page address isn't valid
invalidStartUrl.hint: Start URL #{index} (“{url}”) must be a full address starting with http:// or https://.

noFields.title: Nothing to scrape yet
noFields.hint: Open a page and add at least one field or container.

emptySelector.title: An element has no selector
emptySelector.hint: Pick it on the page again, or remove it.
emptySelector.hintNamed: Pick “{name}” on the page again, or remove it.

duplicateFieldNames.title: Two fields have the same name
duplicateFieldNames.hint: Give each field its own name: {names}.

invalidRegex.title: A transformation's pattern isn't valid
invalidRegex.hint: Check the pattern of the “Regex extract” step in {field}.

invalidEnvVarName.title: “{name}” is not a valid variable name
invalidEnvVarName.hint: Use letters, digits and underscores only, and don't start with a digit.

envVar.startsWithDigit: “{name}” can't start with a digit — use a name like SMTP_PASSWORD.
envVar.invalidChars: “{name}” has characters a variable name can't have — use only letters, digits and underscores (no spaces or dashes).
envVar.generateBlocked: Fix the environment variable name first: {message}
envVar.testValuePlaceholder: Test value (only for the trial run, never saved)

jsonPathPicker.chooseResponse: Which recorded response should the path be picked from?
jsonPathPicker.treeTruncated: A very large response — only the first part is shown.

hint.group: Click the list or object this group should run over. The path is relative to the parent group; inside a list, add a group of its own.
hint.leaf: Click the value to read. A list is shown through its first item.
hint.body: Click the field of the request body that takes the cursor (empty on the first page).

message.noRecording: Nothing recorded to pick from. Record the request first (Start recording on the idle screen, then load the page again), or type the path.
message.truncated: This response was too large to keep in full, so it can't be shown here. Type the path instead.
message.notJson: This is not a JSON response — type the path instead.
message.skipped: The body of this request could not be recorded (not JSON text) — type the path instead.
message.scopeMissing: The parent group was not found in this response — pick another recorded response or type the path.
message.nothingToPick: Nothing to pick here — this response has no matching value.
message.embeddedMissing: The page's embedded JSON was not found any more — reload the page, or type the path.
message.noBody: No request body was recorded for this request — type the path instead.

reason.badKey: This key contains a dot or a bracket, which a path can't express.
reason.bodyNoArrays: A body path can't go through a list.
